subject: Acme private deployment - tenant QoS, surge admission, and eviction proposal
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acme private deployment - initial sizing ask

Dylan —

Acme's infra team (cc'd) asked us to propose a tenant-aware sizing plan for their private GPU pool. They expect a mix of latency-sensitive chat traffic and batched embeddings. Key asks from their side: a conservative minimum throughput guarantee per tenant, a warm-pool strategy for predictable cold-starts, and a way to prevent noisy-tenant impact on others (NIC oversubscription risk).

Can you sketch a short proposal that includes:
- a baseline throughput target (tokens/s and concurrent requests) for a 32-GPU pool (A100 equivalent)
- admission-control design (tokens/queues) and eviction heuristics for prefix/KV cache when under pressure
- an egress NIC oversubscription mitigation — suggested NIC allocation and policing rules

I attached a quick SLO matrix template — fill in where helpful and we can iterate with Acme tomorrow.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Dedicated & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme private deployment - initial sizing ask

Thanks Laura — looping Jonas for kernel/warm-cache detail. Marta, quick clarifying Qs before we run numbers:

1) Traffic shape: is the chat traffic mostly open-domain short-turn (median 30 tokens, p95 250) or long-form generation?
2) Embedding batch sizes and expected throughput (batches/min and points/batch)?
3) Any regulatory constraints on caching (e.g., per-tenant cache partitioning)?

Prelim thinking for a 32x A100-ish cluster:
- Baseline target: 12k tokens/s aggregate steady state (conservative). That maps to ~375 tokens/s per GPU. With multiplexing and batching we can hit higher peaks but we hold 12k as guaranteed throughput for SLA calculations.
- Concurrency target: support 600 active rps (short requests) with 95th latency budget 300ms; longer jobs will use a secondary lane and lower priority.
- Warm-pool: reserve a 10% warm pool (3 GPUs) with priority admission and a pre-warmed KV snapshot per high-volume tenant. Warm-pool can be floored to 6% when utilization >85%.

I'll draft the admission-control token bucket and eviction heuristics and attach the model workbook.

-Dylan
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>
Date: 2028-02-15T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme private deployment - initial sizing ask

Dylan / Laura — some nitty-gritty details to include in the proposal (from runtime perspective):

- KV cache eviction: Prefer tenant-isolated LRU windows combined with a global age-based eviction when the pool-wide KV capacity reaches 92%. This prevents a single tenant with heavy prefix usage from thrashing others. We should expose a per-tenant cache soft-quota (percent of total) and enforce via admission control when soft quota repeatedly exceeded.

- Admission control tokens: Issue tokens per logical request that represent estimated GPU token cost rather than requests. Token cost = estimated response length * per-token compute weight. This lets us favor short-chat traffic by giving it a lower token cost; embeddings batches will consume large tokens but go into a batch lane with lower priority.

- KV warm snapshots: store per-tenant condensed KV checkpoint every 15 minutes. Warm-pool GPUs keep the latest snapshot and hydrate KV on promotion to avoid full cold penalty. Snapshot size estimates: high-volume tenant ~ 200MB; medium ~ 40MB. Ensure disk IO and DRAM overhead accounted for.

I'll add sample numbers to the workbook. Also: NIC oversubscription — we should recommend dedicated 100Gbps per 8 GPUs zone, with host-level egress policing at 80% to allow headroom.

-Jonas
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-16T09:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme private deployment - initial sizing ask

Thanks — answers inline:
1) Chat traffic is mostly short-turn (median ~28 tokens) with occasional long-form (p95 ~400 tokens). About 70% chat, 30% batch embeddings.
2) Embedding batches: 40 batches/hr, each batch ~512 vectors (small batch).
3) No strict regulatory block on caching; we prefer per-tenant encryption at rest and clear audit logs.

Also, our ops team prefers not to reserve >8% of GPUs for warm-pool permanently — they'd rather dynamic warm staging. Could you show a dynamic warm-pool policy where warm capacity scales from 0–12% based on 30m lookback of surge probability?

Marta

--
Marta Ruiz
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-16T13:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme private deployment - initial sizing ask

Marta — thanks for the profile. Attached is a filled SLO matrix and a mutual action plan:
- Week 0: sizing sign-off (this thread)
- Week 1: staging cluster build + warm-snapshot plumbing (runbook included)
- Week 2: soak tests with synthetic surge generator (3x expected peak)
- Week 3: controlled cutover with canary traffic, telemetry evaluation

Key policy decisions for sign-off:
- Baseline SLA: 12k tokens/s aggregate as proposed (we show headroom to 18k with autoscaling).
- Dynamic warm-pool: recommended policy uses a 30-minute surge probability estimator (EWMA of recent QPS spikes) to scale warm GPUs between 0–12% of pool; floor 1 GPU when steady state >20% utilization to avoid cold-start churn.
- NIC policy: allocate 100Gbps per 8-GPU rack; egress policing at 80% with per-tenant shaping for heavy exporters.

Please review the attached workbook (quiet_period_surge_model.xlsx) — it contains the dynamic warm-pool simulation outputs and suggested token-bucket parameters for admission control. If acceptable we'll schedule a joint runbook review with Acme ops tomorrow.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Dedicated & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@acmeops.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-17T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme private deployment - final notes and runbook slot

All — thanks for the quick responses. Action items before today's runbook:
- Acme ops: confirm preferred canary traffic window (we offered 2–4am UTC) and provide contact for emergency page.
- Redwood infra: we'll finalize token bucket cost function in the workbook and attach the admission-control config snippet to the Confluence page.
- Jonas: please prepare the KV snapshot size validation (sample dumps) and a warm-pool promotion timeline (expected hydrate <6s).

I've scheduled a 60-minute runbook review for 2028-02-18 09:00 PT (invite sent). If no objections to the baseline SLA or dynamic warm-pool policy, we'll mark sizing sign-off in HubSpot and start staging.

-Dylan
